question.title: Identifying Consecutive Logins
question.desc: Given a table of user logins, identify the users who have logged in for three consecutive days.
question.setup: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS logins; CREATE TABLE logins (user_id INT, login_date DATE); INSERT INTO logins (user_id, login_date) VALUES (1, '2022-01-01'), (1, '2022-01-02'), (1, '2022-01-03'), (2, '2022-01-01'), (2, '2022-01-03'), (2, '2022-01-05');
question.solution: WITH ranked_logins AS ( SELECT user_id, login_date, DATE_TRUNC('day', login_date) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_date) AS rank FROM logins ) SELECT user_id FROM ranked_logins GROUP BY user_id, rank HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
question.tips: Consider using window functions to assign a rank to each login date for each user.
hints: You'll need to use a window function to assign a rank to each login date.
Consider using a Common Table Expression (CTE) to simplify your query.
Use the `DATE_TRUNC` function to remove the time component from the login date and then subtract the row number from it to get a rank.
